1. get_molecule_profile(smiles: string)

2. analyze_functional_groups(smiles: string)
   Identify functional groups and chemical motifs with fragment SMILES and attachment points.

3. analyze_ring_systems(smiles: string)
   Analyze ring topology: sizes, heteroatom content, aromaticity, and flags for PAH, macrocycle, spiro, and bridgehead features.

4. assess_adme_properties(smiles: string, ph: number)
   Predict pKa, ionization state, logD, and solubility (pKa → ionization → logD → permeability).

5. screen_structural_alerts(smiles: string)
   Screen for toxicophores and structural alerts with mechanistic categories (e.g. Michael acceptors, alkylating agents, PAH). Includes ToxAlerts endpoint patterns and pharmacophore feature counts.

6. remove_salts(smiles: string)
   Strip salts and counterions, keeping the largest organic fragment. Use when SMILES contains '.' separators.

7. predict_metabolites(smiles: string)
   Predict top CYP450 metabolites (Phase 1 and Phase 2) with reaction types and priority scores.

8. get_3d_properties(smiles: string)
   Compute 3D conformer properties: exposed polar surface area (ePSA) and shape (PMI rod/disc/sphere).

9. find_similar_molecules_bbb(smiles: string)
   Find nearest neighbors from BBB_Martins training set with labels and contrastive example.

Structural Alerts (12 categories):

1. Aniline / aromatic amine

2. Alkylating agent
Can transfer alkyl groups to DNA bases, causing mutations.
Matched alerts (8): alkyl_halide [CCl], primary_halide_sulfate [CCl], Alkyl_halides [CCl], R1 Reactive alkyl halides [CCl], Filter1_2_halo_ether [NCCCl], Filter26_alkyl_halide [NCCCl], Filter84_nitrogen_mustard [NCCCl], mustards [NCCCl]

3. Ester / phenol ester / carbonate
Esters can be hydrolyzed to release active metabolites; phenol esters and carbonates may indicate prodrug instability.
Matched alerts (1): Ester [COC(C)=O]

4. Long aliphatic chain
Molecules with long alkyl chains (>=7 carbons) tend to be non-specific membrane disruptors with poor drug-likeness.
Matched alerts (1): Long aliphatic chain [CCCCOCC]

5. Skin sensitization
Structural alerts for skin sensitization via haptenation (covalent binding to skin proteins).
Matched alerts (2): Haloalkanes [CCl], Haloalkanes [Cl]

6. Genotoxic carcinogenicity / mutagenicity
DNA-reactive motifs that cause mutations via direct genotoxic mechanisms.
Matched alerts (8): Aliphatic halide (general) [CCl], Nitrogen and sulphur mustard (specific) [NCCCl], S or N mustard [ClCCNCCCl], Aliphatic halogens [CCl], Haloethylamines [cN(C)CCCl], α-Haloethyl N, S - mustards [ClCCNCCCl], Aromatic and aliphatic substituted primary alkyl halides [CCCl], Aromatic amines [cN]

7. Reactive / unstable / toxic groups
Generally reactive or unstable functional groups flagged across multiple toxicity endpoints.
Matched alerts (7): α-Haloamines [NCCCl], Alkylhalides [CCl], Alkyl halides [CCl], Carboxylic acid esters [CCOC(C)=O], N,N-Dialkyl aniline derivatives (5) [Cc1ccc(N(C)C)cc1], Alkyl Halides [CCl], Simple anilines and phenols [c]

8. Acute aquatic toxicity
Structural features associated with acute toxicity to aquatic organisms, indicating general ecotoxicity and bioactivity.
Matched alerts (2): Haloethyl amines (N-mustard) [NCCCl], Alkyl halide [CCCl]

9. Electrophilic agents
Electrophilic centers that can react with biological nucleophiles (protein thiols, DNA bases).
Matched alerts (1): Mustards [NCCCl]

10. Reactive metabolite formation (idiosyncratic toxicity)
Can form reactive metabolites via CYP metabolism that covalently modify liver proteins, triggering immune-mediated hepatotoxicity.
Matched alerts (1): Anilines, anilides [CN(C)c1ccccc1]

11. Promiscuous compounds
Structural motifs associated with non-specific activity across many biological targets (frequent hitters).
Matched alerts (1): primary_halide_sulfate [CCl]

12. Non-genotoxic carcinogenicity
Promotes cancer through non-DNA-reactive mechanisms (receptor activation, epigenetic changes, chronic inflammation).
Matched alerts (2): S or N mustard [ClCCNCCCl], Aliphatic halogens [CCl]
